size.note: Adults 5.5-13 cm snout to vent (most 6-11 cm), squat and broad, warty, with large oval parotoid glands; no tail. Built at 0.10 m snout to vent (0.102 m in all), the trunk 6 cm across (8.9 cm with the legs folded out), the back 4 cm up at mid-body, the eyes 4.4 cm up; crouched on its belly (2 mm clearance). length_m here is snout to vent; shoulder_or_wingspan_m is the back's height.

source.prompt: A western toad (Anaxyrus boreas), NOT a frog, NOT a cartoon. One adult sitting on the ground in a neutral crouch, side-on pose, the four legs folded under it, the front feet planted. Realistic proportions: 10 cm long, a squat broad warty body, a blunt rounded head with big oval parotoid glands behind the eyes, golden eyes with horizontal pupils, short thick legs. Olive-grey to greenish brown skin with dark warts ringed in rusty brown, a thin pale cream stripe down the middle of the back, a pale mottled belly. No base, no ground. Game-ready, clean closed mesh.

attributes: _BLUE (0 everywhere: no blue patches; kept so the shader path is the lizard's)
tiers.note: The generated crouch kept; the warts found on the full mesh (each vertex's height over its neighbours' mean along the normal) and carried through the collapse in a vertex group: dark faces at the wart peaks (and a hashed few), rusty rings on their neighbours (fewer on lod1, none on lod2). The mid-dorsal stripe is a cream ribbon 2.8 mm wide laid 0.4 mm over the decimated back (26 stations on lod0, 10 on lod1, none on lod2), its stations cast onto each tier. lod0 = 1,134 body + 50 stripe + 16 pupils; lod1 = 382 + 18; lod2 = 120 (the collapse finished without symmetry; the legs fold into the body). GLB 227,108 bytes.

rig: reptile template (as tools/build_salamander.py; to be drawn with the salamanders' slow walk constants): BODY 0, LEG_A 1 (left fore, right hind) and LEG_B 2 (right fore, left hind), pivots on the body's side at the shoulder and the hip; the limbs are smooth-weighted regions of the crouch (the fore legs below and outside the chest and the fore feet planted ahead under the head; the folded hind legs outside the trunk's taper behind), so the small swing never tears the skin; HEAD 6 (pivot at the neck, behind the parotoids); a toad has no tail, so TAIL 3 and TAIL_TIP 8 are tiny stub regions at the vent (about 30 and 20 vertices on lod0; pivots at the vent and 1 mm behind it; lod2 keeps only the tip stub). extras.rig (kind 'reptile'): head, tail, tail_tip, fore, hind, legs (FL FR HL HR), snout_z 0.0585, vent_z -0.0415, tail_end_z -0.4415 (5 snout-vent lengths behind the snout, not the vent: the spine wave's envelope then stays near envS along the body, a sway of a few mm, no bend), belly_y, back_y, drop, blue_off and throat_off (the belly cream), length_m 0.10 (snout to vent). The lead may also set k.wave lower (e.g. 0.004) for the toad. No skin.
accuracy_notes: Reads as a western toad: squat, broad and warty, crouched on its belly with the fore feet planted; olive-grey to greenish brown (two tones hashed), dark warts ringed rusty brown over the back, flanks and legs, the thin pale cream mid-dorsal stripe from behind the eyes to the vent, golden eyes with a dark horizontal pupil (lod0), a pale cream belly mottled grey. Still open: the warts on the decimated skin are faces, not bumps (the collapse smooths the generator's warts away), and the rusty rings are whole neighbouring faces; the parotoid glands are a slightly paler ellipsoid region but read weakly; the limbs are regions with pivots set by eye (no joint chain), so a long stride would smear the folded hind leg; lod2 (120 triangles) loses the legs into a squat lump. The walk will need a toad's slow crawl and hop, not the salamander's sprawl, eventually.
